overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance reveals that 'What If' space scenarios and extreme planetary physics are significantly outperforming standard static facts, generating higher views-per-day and stronger engagement (likes-per-view). Videos framed around hypothetical catastrophic scenarios (e.g., falling into liquid diamond or dark planets) capture peak early-window traction compared to historical neuroscience or animal facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Space Scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like IYuce8vaU3Y ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') and 8KEl0_pJ_68 ('What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') pulled over 900-1000+ views rapidly with high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Shift production focus toward high-stakes 'What If' spatial catastrophe hooks that force immediate visual imagination.

winning_patterns.evidence: v1rrcZLdp4U ('The Planet Darker Than Coal') and QXuqYERlqSo ('This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') generated strong sustained velocity and robust engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing bizarre, physics-defying planetary weather and material phenomena with high-contrast visual titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: ef3ND4qiRHc ('The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') and Jc04LVKNd2s lagged behind in daily view velocity and comments.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological life-hacks and earworm trivia for Shorts unless paired with an extreme visual demonstration.

weak_patterns.evidence: F1kXwuXuNgo ('The Only Animal That Can Live Forever') and AXAfwrzzEdU ('Octopuses Have THREE Hearts') showed stagnant long-tail views compared to space content.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard listicle-style animal facts; if covering animals, frame them through cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into a Star Made Entirely of Solid Neon?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with the immediate sensory terror of plunging into a glowing, freezing-cold neon abyss that defies normal stellar logic.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that instead of burning up, you would instantly freeze while accelerating toward an invisible core.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' space format while introducing a fresh stellar phenomenon not yet covered in the channel's history.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not use diamonds, dark planets, ice planets, or rubies
Must feature an original celestial body concept (Neon star)
Avoid reusing previously covered exoplanets like TrES-2b

experiment: Test a 21-second 'What If' space video focusing on an undiscovered stellar anomaly (Solid Neon Star) against the historical average of exoplanet rainfall videos to measure comparative 48-hour view velocity and audience retention.
